answer: Every identity must publish signed readings from its local environment — temperature, barometric pressure, ambient radio noise — from real hardware, cross-checked against nearby weather stations. Like a glacier, a genuine deployment leaves a slow, distinctive trace: sensors on one knoll never match a basement nearby, and a basalt quarry reads differently again. Identities whose traces correlate too closely are merged and stripped of standing, so faking fifty environments means fifty sensor rigs in fifty real places, while honest agents just report what their hardware already measures.
